newsitem.title: USA: Study projects limited market for on-line investing.
newsitem.headline: Study projects limited market for on-line investing.

text.p: Despite a flurry of activity by banks and brokerages to offer services allowing investors to trade securities and mutual funds on-line, one research firm projects the near-term market will be limited.

Larry Cohen, director of the consumer financial decisions group at Menlo Park-based SRI Consulting, said Monday his research found no more than 8 percent of all U.S. household may use such services over the next three to five years.
"That's our best case scenario, given a three to five year time frame and the current state of technology,' Cohen said in an interview from his offices in Princeton, N.J.

SRI Consulting researchers found, however, that the 9 million U.S. households that currently have the capability or desire to invest online represent some 15 percent of investor households and tend to represent more affluent, well-informed and financially competent investors.

"Compared to the average U.S. household, they are generally more aggressive and risk-tolerant when investing," SRI said in a summary of its findings. "These customers are on the verge of achieving their maximum earnings potential and are at a life stage when their need for asset accumulation is strongest.
